name: Gitleaks secret scan
description: Finds API keys, tokens, passwords and private keys committed in source files, with Gitleaks' rules (or the repository's own .gitleaks.toml) plus SiegeKit's rules for Supabase keys. Secret values are redacted by the tool and masked again by SiegeKit.

run.gitleaksRules:
[[rules]]
id = "siegekit-supabase-secret-key"
description = "Supabase secret key (sb_secret_)"
regex = '''\b(sb_secret_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,})'''
entropy = 3
keywords = ["sb_secret_"]
# The Supabase CLI's fixed key for local stacks (supabase/cli,
# packages/stack/src/Defaults.ts) is public, so it is not a leak.
# Written as a pattern so that the key itself is not in this file,
# with the class early so that the rule does not match its own
# pattern (SiegeKit's self-scan, ADR 0063).
# Gitleaks' generic-api-key rule still reports it on a line such as
# SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY=..., as it did before this rule (ADR 0063).
# The CLI's publishable key is not left out: it is reported as info
# like any publishable key, and leaving it out would let Gitleaks'
# generic-api-key rule report it as a high leak instead (ADR 0063).
[[rules.allowlists]]
regexTarget = "match"
regexes = ['''sb_secret_N7UND0Ug[j]KTVK-Uodkm0Hg_xSvEMPvz''']

[[rules]]
id = "siegekit-supabase-publishable-key"
description = "Supabase publishable key (sb_publishable_)"
regex = '''\b(sb_publishable_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,})'''
entropy = 3
keywords = ["sb_publishable_"]
